stem: A client who smokes cigarettes says, “I want to quit but I cannot afford private counseling.” Which evidence-based resource should the nurse recommend?

options.A: Recommend switching to another combustible tobacco product, because changing products is an evidence-based substitute for tobacco cessation.
options.B: Recommend 1-800-QUIT-NOW, which connects callers to free, confidential quitline counseling and individualized tobacco-cessation support today.
options.C: Advise the client to wait until private counseling is affordable, because free telephone-based cessation services are not available nationwide.
options.D: Advise attempting cessation without counseling or medication, because professional support does not improve the likelihood of successful quitting.

rationale: CDC identifies 1-800-QUIT-NOW as a nationwide quitline resource that provides free, confidential coaching and tobacco-cessation support. CDC also notes that counseling and medication together give the best chance of quitting successfully. Option B directly addresses the client's cost barrier with an evidence-based resource. The other choices either substitute continued combustible-tobacco use, incorrectly deny nationwide free quitline services, or dismiss effective cessation support.
educational_objective: Refer clients who want to quit tobacco to free, confidential evidence-based quitline support such as 1-800-QUIT-NOW.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Quitlines and Other Cessation Support Resources / How to Quit Smoking
source_version_date: Quitlines page 2025-01-31; How to Quit Smoking 2024-05-15
source_locator: Quitlines: services are free, confidential, tailored, available nationwide via 1-800-QUIT-NOW; How to Quit Smoking: counseling and medication together provide the best chance of quitting.
source_claim_supported: CDC states that 1-800-QUIT-NOW connects callers nationwide to free, confidential quitline counseling/support and that evidence-based cessation support improves quit success.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — risk-reduction teaching, preventive care, and health-promotion resources.
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — tobacco cessation

source_original.rationale: CDC identifies 1-800-QUIT-NOW as a nationwide resource that provides free, confidential quitline counseling and cessation support. Option B is correct. Option A substitutes another combustible tobacco product for cessation. Option C incorrectly claims free nationwide telephone cessation services are unavailable. Option D incorrectly states that counseling or medication support does not improve quit success.
source_original.source_detail: CDC — How to Quit Smoking / Quitlines: 1-800-QUIT-NOW connects callers to free, confidential quitline coaching and cessation support; counseling and cessation medications improve quit success. Current CDC tobacco-cessation guidance; quitline information updated/rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Health Promotion and Maintenance: preventive care, screening, age-appropriate health promotion and risk-reduction teaching activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the construct and answer key. Updated the primary source to CDC's dedicated current quitline resource while preserving the current How to Quit Smoking guidance as corroboration.

audit_findings.currentness: CDC quitline resource dated 2025-01-31 and live guidance rechecked 2026-08-16.
audit_findings.exact_locator: CDC explicitly lists 1-800-QUIT-NOW as free, confidential and nationwide.
audit_findings.claim_audit: No promise of free medication for every caller was added; the item only claims free confidential quitline counseling/support.

distractor_audit.A: Continues combustible-tobacco exposure rather than cessation.
distractor_audit.B: Directly matches CDC guidance and the cost constraint.
distractor_audit.C: False because quitlines are nationwide and free to callers.
distractor_audit.D: False because counseling and medications are evidence-based cessation supports.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B directly provides a free evidence-based nationwide resource.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices address the client's stated financial barrier and quitting strategy.
audit_findings.blueprint: Fits preventive health promotion and risk-reduction teaching.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Second pass checked the scope of 'free'; final wording limits this to quitline services rather than universally free medication.
